sanskrit: suhanur durmukhaḥ śaṅkhaḥ sumanāḥ sumatiḥ svanaḥ ghaṭodaro mahāpārśvaḥ krathanaḥ piṭharas tathā
english: Suhanu, Durmukha, Śaṅkha, Sumanā, Sumati, Svana, Ghaṭodara, Mahāpārśva, Krathana, and likewise Piṭhara —

sanskrit: viśvarūpaḥ surūpaś ca virūpo 'tha mahāśirāḥ daśagrīvaś ca vālī ca meghavāsā daśāvaraḥ
english: Viśvarūpa, Surūpa, Virūpa, Mahāśiras, Daśagrīva, Vālī, Meghavāsā, and Daśāvara —

sanskrit: kaiṭabho viṭaṭūtaś ca saṃhrādaś cendratāpanaḥ daityadānavasaṃghāś ca sarve rucirakuṇḍalāḥ
english: Kaiṭabha, Viṭaṭūta, Saṃhrāda, and Indratāpana — all these hosts of Daityas and Dānavas, wearing beautiful earrings,

sanskrit: sragviṇo maulinaḥ sarve tathā divyaparicchadāḥ sarve labdhavarāḥ śūrāḥ sarve vigatamṛtyavaḥ
english: all garlanded, all wearing crowns, all adorned with divine ornaments, all having obtained boons, all heroes, all free from death —

sanskrit: te tasyāṃ varuṇaṃ devaṃ dharmapāśasthitāḥ sadā upāsate mahātmānaṃ sarve sucaritavratāḥ
english: they, stationed by the noose of righteousness, ever attend upon the god Varuṇa in that hall, all great-souled and firm in virtuous vows.

sanskrit: tathā samudrāś catvāro nadī bhāgīrathī ca yā kālindī vidiśā veṇṇā narmadā vegavāhinī
english: Likewise the four oceans, the river Bhāgīrathī, Kālindī, Vidiśā, Veṇṇā, and the swift-flowing Narmadā —

sanskrit: vipāśā ca śatadruś ca candrabhāgā sarasvatī irāvatī vitastā ca sindhur devanadas tathā
english: Vipāśā, Śatadrū, Candrabhāgā, Sarasvatī, Irāvatī, Vitastā, the Sindhu, and the divine river Devanadat —

sanskrit: godāvarī kṛṣṇaveṇṇā kāverī ca saridvarā etāś cānyāś ca saritas tīrthāni ca sarāṃsi ca
english: Godāvarī, Kṛṣṇaveṇṇā, the noble river Kāverī — these and other rivers, as well as holy fords and lakes,

sanskrit: kūpāś ca saprasravaṇā dehavanto yudhiṣṭhira palvalāni taḍāgāni dehavanty atha bhārata
english: wells with springs, O Yudhiṣṭhira, embodied pools and tanks, O Bhārata — all having taken bodily form —

sanskrit: diśas tathā mahī caiva tathā sarve mahīdharāḥ upāsate mahātmānaṃ sarve jalacarās tathā
english: the directions, the earth itself, all the mountains, and all aquatic creatures — they attend upon that great-souled one.

sanskrit: gītavāditravantaś ca gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ stuvanto varuṇaṃ tasyāṃ sarva eva samāsate
english: Troops of Gandharvas and Apsarases, equipped with song and music, praising Varuṇa — all of them assemble in that hall.

sanskrit: mahīdharā ratnavanto rasā yeṣu pratiṣṭhitāḥ sarve vigrahavantas te tam īśvaram upāsate
english: The mountains bearing precious gems, the subterranean waters in which minerals rest — all of them, having taken form, attend upon that lord.

sanskrit: eṣā mayā saṃpatatā vāruṇī bharatarṣabha dṛṣṭapūrvā sabhā ramyā kuberasya sabhāṃ śṛṇu
english: This lovely hall of Varuṇa was seen by me in passing, O bull of the Bhāratas. Now hear of the hall of Kubera.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca sabhā vaiśravaṇī rājañ śatayojanam āyatā vistīrṇā saptatiś caiva yojanāni sitaprabhā
english: Nārada said: The hall of Vaiśravaṇa, O king, is a hundred yojanas long, seventy yojanas wide, and gleaming white.

sanskrit: tapasā nirmitā rājan svayaṃ vaiśravaṇena sā śaśiprabhā khecarīṇāṃ kailāsaśikharopamā
english: It was fashioned by Vaiśravaṇa himself through asceticism, O king; it has the radiance of the moon, floats in the sky, and resembles the peak of Kailāsa.

sanskrit: guhyakair uhyamānā sā khe viṣakteva dṛśyate divyā hemamayair uccaiḥ pādapair upaśobhitā
english: Borne by Guhyakas, it appears as if suspended in the sky; it is divine and adorned by tall golden trees.

sanskrit: raśmivatī bhāsvarā ca divyagandhā manoramā sitābhraśikharākārā plavamāneva dṛśyate
english: Radiant and luminous, filled with divine fragrance, delightful, shaped like the peak of a white cloud — it appears to float.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ vaiśravaṇo rājā vicitrābharaṇāmbaraḥ strīsahasrāvṛtaḥ śrīmān āste jvalitakuṇḍalaḥ
english: In that hall, King Vaiśravaṇa sits resplendent, wearing ornaments and garments of many kinds, surrounded by thousands of women, his earrings blazing with light.

sanskrit: divākaranibhe puṇye divyāstaraṇasaṃvṛte divyapādopadhāne ca niṣaṇṇaḥ paramāsane
english: He is seated on a supreme throne, holy as the sun itself, spread with divine coverings and furnished with divine footrests.

sanskrit: mandārāṇām udārāṇāṃ vanāni surabhīṇi ca saugandhikānāṃ cādāya gandhān gandhavahaḥ śuciḥ
english: The pure wind, carrying fragrances from the splendid groves of Mandāra trees and from the Saugandhika forests —

sanskrit: nalinyāś cālakākhyāyāś candanānāṃ vanasya ca manohṛdayasaṃhlādī vāyus tam upasevate
english: and from the lotus-ponds of the city named Alakā, and from the sandalwood forests — that breeze, delighting the heart, wafts about him.

sanskrit: tatra devāḥ sagandharvā gaṇair apsarasāṃ vṛtāḥ divyatānena gītāni gānti divyāni bhārata
english: There, O Bhārata, gods together with Gandharvas, surrounded by troops of Apsarases, sing divine songs with divine melodic grace.

sanskrit: miśrakeśī ca rambhā ca citrasenā śucismitā cārunetrā ghṛtācī ca menakā puñjikasthalā
english: Miśrakeśī, Rambhā, Citrasena, Śucismitā, Cārunetrā, Ghṛtācī, Menakā, Puñjikasthalā —

sanskrit: viśvācī sahajanyā ca pramlocā urvaśī irā vargā ca saurabheyī ca samīcī budbudā latā
english: Viśvācī, Sahajanyā, Pramlocā, Urvaśī, Irā, Vargā, Saurabheyī, Samīcī, Budbudā, and Latā —

sanskrit: etāḥ sahasraśaś cānyā nṛttagītaviśāradāḥ upatiṣṭhanti dhanadaṃ pāṇḍavāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: these and thousands of other Apsarases, skilled in dance and song, attend upon Dhanadhada, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: aniśaṃ divyavāditrair nṛttair gītaiś ca sā sabhā aśūnyā rucirā bhāti gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ
english: Unceasingly, with divine music, dance, and song, that hall shines lovely and ever full, thronged with bands of Gandharvas and Apsarases.

sanskrit: kiṃnarā nāma gandharvā narā nāma tathāpare maṇibhadro 'tha dhanadaḥ śvetabhadraś ca guhyakaḥ
english: Among the Gandharvas are the Kiṃnaras by name; others are called Naras. There too are Maṇibhadra, Dhanada, the Guhyaka Śvetabhadra —

sanskrit: kaśerako gaṇḍakaṇḍuḥ pradyotaś ca mahābalaḥ kustumburuḥ piśācaś ca gajakarṇo viśālakaḥ
english: Kaśeraka, Gaṇḍakaṇḍu, the mighty Pradyota, Kustumburu, the Piśāca, Gajakarṇa, and Viśālaka —

sanskrit: varāhakarṇaḥ sāndroṣṭhaḥ phalabhakṣaḥ phalodakaḥ aṅgacūḍaḥ śikhāvarto hemanetro vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Varāhakarṇa, Sāndroṣṭha, Phalabhakṣa, Phalodaka, Aṅgacūḍa, Śikhāvarta, Hemanetra, and Vibhīṣaṇa —

sanskrit: puṣpānanaḥ piṅgalakaḥ śoṇitodaḥ pravālakaḥ vṛkṣavāsyaniketaś ca cīravāsāś ca bhārata
english: Puṣpānana, Piṅgalaka, Śoṇitoda, Pravālaka, one whose home is in the treetops, and Cīravāsā — O Bhārata —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo yakṣāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ sadā bhagavatī ca śrīs tathaiva nalakūbaraḥ
english: these and many other Yakṣas, hundreds of thousands of them, and the blessed goddess Śrī herself, and likewise Nalakūbara —

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca bahuśas tasyāṃ bhavanty anye ca madvidhāḥ ācāryāś cābhavaṃs tatra tathā devarṣayo 'pare
english: and I myself have visited it often, and others like me; teachers were present there, and divine sages as well.

sanskrit: bhagavān bhūtasaṃghaiś ca vṛtaḥ śatasahasraśaḥ umāpatiḥ paśupatiḥ śūladhṛg bhaganetrahā
english: The blessed lord — Umā's husband, Paśupati, bearer of the trident, destroyer of Bhaga's eyes —

sanskrit: tryambako rājaśārdūla devī ca vigataklamā vāmanair vikaṭaiḥ kubjaiḥ kṣatajākṣair manojavaiḥ
english: three-eyed Tryambaka, O tiger among kings, and the Devī free from fatigue — surrounded by dwarfs, hideous beings, hunchbacks, red-eyed ones, and beings swift as the mind —

sanskrit: māṃsamedovasāhārair ugraśravaṇadarśanaiḥ nānāpraharaṇair ghorair vātair iva mahājavaiḥ vṛtaḥ sakhāyam anvāste sadaiva dhanadaṃ nṛpa
english: by those who eat flesh, fat, and marrow, terrible to hear and to see, bearing various dreadful weapons, swift as the wind — thus attended, he ever sits with his friend Dhanada, O king.

sanskrit: sā sabhā tādṛśī rājan mayā dṛṣṭāntarikṣagā pitāmahasabhāṃ rājan kathayiṣye gataklamām
english: Such was the hall I saw floating in the sky, O king. Now, O king, I shall describe the hall of the Grandsire, free from all fatigue.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca purā devayuge rājann ādityo bhagavān divaḥ āgacchan mānuṣaṃ lokaṃ didṛkṣur vigataklamaḥ
english: Nārada said: Long ago, O king, in the age of the gods, the blessed Āditya descended from heaven to the world of men, free from fatigue, wishing to see it.

sanskrit: caran mānuṣarūpeṇa sabhāṃ dṛṣṭvā svayaṃbhuvaḥ sabhām akathayan mahyaṃ brāhmīṃ tattvena pāṇḍava
english: Roaming in human form, having seen the hall of Svayambhū, he described to me truly that Brāhmic hall, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: aprameyaprabhāṃ divyāṃ mānasīṃ bharatarṣabha anirdeśyāṃ prabhāvena sarvabhūtamanoramām
english: That hall is of immeasurable splendor, divine, born of the mind, O bull of the Bhāratas, indescribable in its power, and charming to all beings.

sanskrit: śrutvā guṇān ahaṃ tasyāḥ sabhāyāḥ pāṇḍunandana darśanepsus tathā rājann ādityam aham abruvam
english: Hearing of the qualities of that hall, O son of Pāṇḍu, I desired to see it, and so, O king, I addressed Āditya:

sanskrit: bhagavan draṣṭum icchāmi pitāmahasabhām aham yena sā tapasā śakyā karmaṇā vāpi gopate
english: "Blessed one, I wish to see the hall of the Grandsire. By what asceticism, O lord of cattle, or by what deed is it possible to see it?

sanskrit: auṣadhair vā tathā yuktair uta vā māyayā yayā tan mamācakṣva bhagavan paśyeyaṃ tāṃ sabhāṃ katham
english: Or by what efficacious herbs, or by what magical power? Tell me, O blessed one — how might I see that hall?"

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān sūryo mām upādāya vīryavān agacchat tāṃ sabhāṃ brāhmīṃ vipāpāṃ vigataklamām
english: Then that mighty, blessed Sūrya, taking me with him, went to that Brāhmic hall, free from sin and from all fatigue.

sanskrit: evaṃrūpeti sā śakyā na nirdeṣṭuṃ janādhipa kṣaṇena hi bibharty anyad anirdeśyaṃ vapus tathā
english: "It is of such-and-such a form" — even so it cannot be described, O lord of men, for from moment to moment it assumes another form that is equally beyond description.

sanskrit: na veda parimāṇaṃ vā saṃsthānaṃ vāpi bhārata na ca rūpaṃ mayā tādṛg dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ kadā cana
english: I know not its dimensions, nor its configuration, O Bhārata; nor have I ever before seen a form like it.

sanskrit: susukhā sā sabhā rājan na śītā na ca gharmadā na kṣutpipāse na glāniṃ prāpya tāṃ prāpnuvanty uta
english: That hall is supremely pleasant, O king — neither cold nor hot; those who enter it experience no hunger, no thirst, and no weariness.

sanskrit: nānārūpair iva kṛtā suvicitraiḥ subhāsvaraiḥ stambhair na ca dhṛtā sā tu śāśvatī na ca sā kṣarā
english: It seems fashioned of many forms, wonderfully varied and brilliantly luminous; it is not supported by pillars; it is eternal and does not decay.

sanskrit: ati candraṃ ca sūryaṃ ca śikhinaṃ ca svayaṃprabhā dīpyate nākapṛṣṭhasthā bhāsayantīva bhāskaram
english: Shining by its own light, it blazes beyond the moon, the sun, and fire; stationed in the vault of heaven, it seems to outshine even the sun.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ sa bhagavān āste vidadhad devamāyayā svayam eko 'niśaṃ rājaṃl lokāṃl lokapitāmahaḥ
english: In that hall, the blessed Grandsire of the worlds sits alone, unceasingly governing the worlds through divine power.

sanskrit: upatiṣṭhanti cāpy enaṃ prajānāṃ patayaḥ prabhum dakṣaḥ pracetāḥ pulaho marīciḥ kaśyapas tathā
english: The lords of creatures also attend upon him as their master: Dakṣa, Pracetas, Pulaha, Marīci, and likewise Kaśyapa —

sanskrit: bhṛgur atrir vasiṣṭhaś ca gautamaś ca tathāṅgirāḥ mano 'ntarikṣaṃ vidyāś ca vāyus tejo jalaṃ mahī
english: Bhṛgu, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, and Aṅgiras; Mind, Space, the Sciences, Wind, Fire, Water, and Earth —

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśas tathā rūpaṃ raso gandhaś ca bhārata prakṛtiś ca vikāraś ca yac cānyat kāraṇaṃ bhuvaḥ
english: Sound, Touch, Form, Taste, and Smell, O Bhārata; Primordial Nature, its modifications, and whatever other causes exist in the world —

sanskrit: candramāḥ saha nakṣatrair ādityaś ca gabhastimān vāyavaḥ kratavaś caiva saṃkalpaḥ prāṇa eva ca
english: the Moon together with the lunar mansions, the radiant Āditya, the winds, the sacred rites, Resolve, and the vital breath —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ svayaṃbhuvam upasthitāḥ artho dharmaś ca kāmaś ca harṣo dveṣas tapo damaḥ
english: these and many others are present before Svayambhū; Artha, Dharma, and Kāma; Joy, Aversion, Austerity, and Self-restraint —

sanskrit: āyānti tasyāṃ sahitā gandharvāpsarasas tathā viṃśatiḥ sapta caivānye lokapālāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Gandharvas and Apsarases come there together, twenty-seven of the other kinds, and all the guardians of the worlds in every direction.

sanskrit: śukro bṛhaspatiś caiva budho 'ṅgāraka eva ca śanaiścaraś ca rāhuś ca grahāḥ sarve tathaiva ca
english: Śukra, Bṛhaspati, Budha, Aṅgāraka, Śanaiścara, Rāhu, and all the planets likewise —

sanskrit: mantro rathaṃtaraś caiva harimān vasumān api ādityāḥ sādhirājāno nānādvaṃdvair udāhṛtāḥ
english: Mantra, Rathaṃtara, Harimān, Vasumān, the Ādityas with their king — designated by the various pairs of names —

sanskrit: maruto viśvakarmā ca vasavaś caiva bhārata tathā pitṛgaṇāḥ sarve sarvāṇi ca havīṃṣy atha
english: the Maruts, Viśvakarman, the Vasus, O Bhārata, all the hosts of Pitṛs, and all the oblations —

sanskrit: ṛgvedaḥ sāmavedaś ca yajurvedaś ca pāṇḍava atharvavedaś ca tathā parvāṇi ca viśāṃ pate
english: the Ṛgveda, the Sāmaveda, the Yajurveda, O Pāṇḍava, and likewise the Atharvaveda, and the sacred junctures of time, O lord of the people —

sanskrit: itihāsopavedāś ca vedāṅgāni ca sarvaśaḥ grahā yajñāś ca somaś ca daivatāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: the Itihāsas, the Upavedas, and all the Vedāṅgas, the planets, the sacrifices, Soma, and all the deities —

sanskrit: sāvitrī durgataraṇī vāṇī saptavidhā tathā medhā dhṛtiḥ śrutiś caiva prajñā buddhir yaśaḥ kṣamā
english: the Sāvitrī, the Durgataraṇī, the sevenfold Vāṇī, Intellect, Steadiness, Learning, Wisdom, Understanding, Renown, and Patience —

sanskrit: sāmāni stutiśastrāṇi gāthāś ca vividhās tathā bhāṣyāṇi tarkayuktāni dehavanti viśāṃ pate
english: Sāman hymns, Stuti verses, Śastra recitations, various Gāthā songs, and logical commentaries — all in embodied form, O lord of the people —

sanskrit: kṣaṇā lavā muhūrtāś ca divā rātris tathaiva ca ardhamāsāś ca māsāś ca ṛtavaḥ ṣaṭ ca bhārata
english: Kṣaṇas, Lavas, Muhūrtas, day and night likewise, the fortnights, months, and the six seasons, O Bhārata —

sanskrit: saṃvatsarāḥ pañcayugam ahorātrāś caturvidhāḥ kālacakraṃ ca yad divyaṃ nityam akṣayam avyayam
english: the years, the fivefold Yuga cycle, the four kinds of day-and-night reckonings, and the divine Wheel of Time, eternal, inexhaustible, and unchanging —

sanskrit: aditir ditir danuś caiva surasā vinatā irā kālakā surabhir devī saramā cātha gautamī
english: Aditi, Diti, Danu, Surasā, Vinatā, Irā, Kālakā, the goddess Surabhī, Saramā, and Gautamī —

sanskrit: ādityā vasavo rudrā marutaś cāśvināv api viśvedevāś ca sādhyāś ca pitaraś ca manojavāḥ
english: the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Maruts, the two Aśvins, the Viśvedevas, the Sādhyas, and the swift-minded Pitṛs —

sanskrit: rākṣasāś ca piśācāś ca dānavā guhyakās tathā suparṇanāgapaśavaḥ pitāmaham upāsate
english: Rākṣasas, Piśācas, Dānavas, Guhyakas, Suparṇas, Nāgas, and animals — all attend upon the Grandsire.

sanskrit: devo nārāyaṇas tasyāṃ tathā devarṣayaś ca ye ṛṣayo vālakhilyāś ca yonijāyonijās tathā
english: The god Nārāyaṇa is there, as well as the divine sages, the Vālakhilya sages, and both the womb-born and those not born of wombs.

sanskrit: yac ca kiṃ cit triloke 'smin dṛśyate sthāṇujaṅgamam sarvaṃ tasyāṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ tad viddhi manujādhipa
english: Whatever is seen in these three worlds, moving or stationary — all of it I saw in that hall. Know this, O lord of men.

sanskrit: aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi yatīnām ūrdhvaretasām prajāvatāṃ ca pañcāśad ṛṣīṇām api pāṇḍava
english: Eighty-eight thousand celibate ascetics, O Pāṇḍava, and fifty of the sages who have offspring —

sanskrit: te sma tatra yathākāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve divaukasaḥ praṇamya śirasā tasmai pratiyānti yathāgatam
english: all those celestial beings, having seen him as they wished, bow their heads to him and return by the way they came.

sanskrit: atithīn āgatān devān daityān nāgān munīṃs tathā yakṣān suparṇān kāleyān gandharvāpsarasas tathā
english: Gods, Daityas, Nāgas, sages, Yakṣas, Suparṇas, Kāleyas, Gandharvas, and Apsarases who arrive as guests —

sanskrit: mahābhāgān amitadhīr brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ dayāvān sarvabhūteṣu yathārhaṃ pratipadyate
english: these greatly fortunate ones — Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds, of boundless intelligence and compassionate toward all beings, receives fittingly.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca viśvātmā svayaṃbhūr amitaprabhaḥ sāntvamānārthasaṃbhogair yunakti manujādhipa
english: And having received them, the Soul of the Universe, Svayambhū of immeasurable splendor, engages them with gentle words, honors, and pleasures, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tathā tair upayātaiś ca pratiyātaiś ca bhārata ākulā sā sabhā tāta bhavati sma sukhapradā
english: And so, O Bhārata, with those coming and going, that hall is ever bustling, dear friend, and bestows happiness.

sanskrit: sarvatejomayī divyā brahmarṣigaṇasevitā brāhmyā śriyā dīpyamānā śuśubhe vigataklamā
english: All-luminous, divine, attended by hosts of Brahmarṣis, blazing with Brāhmic glory, free from all fatigue — it shone magnificently.

sanskrit: sā sabhā tādṛśī dṛṣṭā sarvalokeṣu durlabhā sabheyaṃ rājaśārdūla manuṣyeṣu yathā tava
english: Such was that hall I saw — unequalled in all the worlds. Among humans, O tiger among kings, it is like your own hall.

sanskrit: etā mayā dṛṣṭapūrvāḥ sabhā deveṣu pāṇḍava taveyaṃ mānuṣe loke sarvaśreṣṭhatamā sabhā
english: These halls among the gods I have seen before, O Pāṇḍava; yet your hall is the most excellent of all in the world of humans.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca prāyaśo rājalokas te kathito vadatāṃ vara vaivasvatasabhāyāṃ tu yathā vadasi vai prabho
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have described for the most part the company of kings, O best of speakers; and as for the hall of Vaivasvata, as you tell it, O lord —

sanskrit: varuṇasya sabhāyāṃ tu nāgās te kathitā vibho daityendrāś caiva bhūyiṣṭhāḥ saritaḥ sāgarās tathā
english: in the hall of Varuṇa, O mighty one, you spoke of the Nāgas, the great Daitya lords, rivers, and oceans —
